# 2 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The Jews in Jerusalem and those in the land of Judea, to their brothers the Jews in Egypt — greetings and true peace.

**2** May God do good to you and remember his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his faithful servants.

**3** May he give to all of you a heart to worship him and to do his will with a great heart and a willing soul.

**4** May he open your heart in his law and in his commandments and give you peace.

**5** May he hear your prayers and be reconciled with you, and may he not forsake you in an evil time.

**6** And now we ourselves are here praying for you.

**7** In the reign of Demetrius, in the one hundred and sixty-ninth year, we Jews wrote to you in the extreme distress that came upon us in those years, from the time that Jason and his company defected from the holy land and from the kingdom

**8** and burned the gate and shed innocent blood. And we prayed to the LORD, and we were heard; and we offered sacrifice and fine flour; and we lit the lamps; and we set out the bread of the Presence.

**9** And now see that you keep the days of the Feast of Tabernacles in the month of Chislev.

**10** Written in the one hundred and eighty-eighth year, the people who are in Jerusalem and in Judea, and the senate and Judas, to Aristobulus, who is the teacher of Ptolemy the king, who is of the stock of the anointed priests, and to the Jews who are in Egypt — greetings and health.

**11** Having been saved by God out of great perils, we give him great thanks, since we engaged in war against such a king.

**12** For he drove out those who set themselves in array against the holy city.

**13** For when the leader arrived in Persia, and the army with him that seemed irresistible, they were cut to pieces in the temple of Nanea by the treachery of the priests of Nanea.

**14** For Antiochus, on the pretense of marrying her, came to the place together with his friends, in order to receive much money in the name of a dowry.

**15** When the priests of Nanea set it out and he entered with a few people within the precinct of the temple, they closed the temple when Antiochus entered.

**16** And opening the secret door of the ceiling, they threw stones and struck down the leader, and they cut him to pieces and threw the heads to those outside.

**17** Blessed in all things be our God, who delivered up the impious ones.

**18** Since we are about to celebrate the purification of the temple on the twenty-fifth of the month of Chislev, we thought it necessary to notify you, so that you also might celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles and the feast of fire that was given when Nehemiah, who built the temple and the altar, offered sacrifices.

**19** For when our fathers were being led to Persia, the pious priests of that time took some of the fire of the altar secretly and hid it in the hollow of a waterless cistern, where they secured it so that the place was unknown to anyone.

**20** Now after many years had passed, when it pleased God, Nehemiah, having been commissioned by the king of Persia, sent the descendants of the priests who had hidden it to look for the fire. When they reported to us that they found no fire but thick water,

**21** he ordered them to draw it out and bring it to him. And when the sacrificial materials were set in order, Nehemiah commanded the priests to sprinkle the wood and what lay upon it with the water.

**22** When this was done, and some time had passed, and the sun that had been clouded over shone out, a great fire was kindled, so that all marveled.

**23** And while the sacrifice was being consumed, the priests offered prayer — the priests and all of them, with Jonathan leading and the rest responding with Nehemiah.

**24** And the prayer was as follows: "O LORD, LORD God, Creator of all things, who art fearful and strong and just and merciful, who alone art king and art gracious,

**25** who alone art bountiful, who alone art just and almighty and eternal, who savest Israel from every evil, who madest the fathers thy chosen people and sanctifiedst them:

**26** accept the sacrifice on behalf of all thy people Israel and guard thy portion and make it holy.

**27** Gather together our scattered people, set free those who are slaves among the nations, look upon those who are rejected and despised, and let the nations know that thou art our God.

**28** Torment those who oppress us and in arrogance treat us with insolence.

**29** Plant thy people in thy holy place, as Moses said."

**30** And the priests sang the hymns.

**31** And when the sacrifice was consumed, Nehemiah ordered the remaining water to be poured upon large stones.

**32** When this was done, a flame was kindled; but it was consumed by the light that shone back from the altar.

**33** So when the matter became known, and it was reported to the king of the Persians that, in the place where the exiled priests had hidden the fire, water had appeared with which Nehemiah's people had purified the sacrifice,

**34** the king investigated the matter and enclosed the place and made it sacred.

**35** And those with whom the king exchanged many gifts he received generously.

**36** And those around Nehemiah called this thing "Nephthar," which is translated "purification"; but most people call it "naphtha."
